title: A finite type algebra as a compatible system over the base stages
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder and let $F:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ have a colimit cocone $c$ with ring $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $P$ be a commutative $A$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], in the same universe as the rings of $F$. There exist $i_0\in I$, a diagram $D$ of commutative rings on $J=\{i\mid i_0\leq i\}$, maps $\sigma_i:F_i\to D_i$ of finite type, and a ring isomorphism $e:\operatorname{colim}D\simeq P$. For each $i$, $e\circ\iota_i\circ\sigma_i$ is the given composite $F_i\to A\to P$; for $i\leq j$, $D_{ij}\circ\sigma_i=\sigma_j\circ F_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation), construction of the stage algebras; finite-type-only variant using polynomial images instead of descending relations. Agent-written proof of this variant, checked in Lean.

proof.text: Choose a finite set s of algebra generators of P using Algebra.FiniteType.out, and any i₀ in the nonempty preorder. Work on its directed tail. For each i let ρᵢ be Fᵢ → A → P and let Eᵢ be polynomial evaluation Fᵢ[s] → P. Its image Sᵢ is a subring of P.

The cocone identity gives ρⱼ ∘ Fᵢⱼ = ρᵢ. Mapping polynomial coefficients along Fᵢⱼ therefore shows Sᵢ ⊆ Sⱼ, using MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_map_hom. Subring inclusions define a functor D and an inclusion cocone to P. The constants followed by the surjective range restriction of Eᵢ give σᵢ. Polynomial rings in the finite set s are of finite type, so σᵢ is of finite type.

Every element of P lies in some Sᵢ. Prove this by Algebra.adjoin_induction: each chosen generator is the evaluation of its variable at every stage; a base coefficient has a stage representative by Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep applied to c, which can be moved above i₀; sums and products are handled at common upper stages.

The canonical colimit map v: colim D → P is surjective by the union assertion and colimit.ι_desc. If two colimit elements have the same image, represent them at stages, move to a common upper stage, and use equality in the common subring of P. Subtype.ext and colimit.w give their equality in colim D. Thus RingEquiv.ofBijective v gives e. The polynomial evaluation formulas for constants prove both required structure-map equations.

mathlib_searches.query: A finitely generated algebra over a directed colimit of commutative rings is a directed colimit of finite type algebras over the stages
A finite type algebra over a directed colimit of commutative rings is the directed union of subrings generated by its algebra generators and the image of each stage
mathlib_searches.results: FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.exists_fg_substructure_in_Sigma and Algebra.EssFiniteType.finset are nearby, but do not supply the compatible ring system. RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit concerns map equality only.
Algebra.adjoin_eq_ring_closure identifies the generated subring. No ring-system descent theorem.
Algebra.adjoin_eq_ring_closure and Algebra.FiniteType.small supply ingredients. The proof uses polynomial images to avoid expensive conversions between subring and subalgebra ring structures.

theorem exists_finiteType_ring_system
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (P : Type u) [CommRing P] [Algebra c.pt P] [Algebra.FiniteType c.pt P] :
    ∃ i₀ : I, ∃ D : {i : I // i₀ ≤ i} ⥤ CommRingCat.{u},
      ∃ (σ : ∀ i : {i : I // i₀ ≤ i}, F.obj i.1 →+* D.obj i)
        (e : (colimit D : CommRingCat.{u}) ≃+* P),
        (∀ i, (σ i).FiniteType) ∧
        (∀ i, e.toRingHom.comp ((colimit.ι D i).hom.comp (σ i)) =
          (algebraMap c.pt P).comp (c.ι.app i.1).hom) ∧
        (∀ (i j : {i : I // i₀ ≤ i}) (h : i ≤ j),
          (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom.comp (σ i) =
            (σ j).comp (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom)
